label: Speech & Acoustic Lab, Faculty of Engineering, Bar-Ilan University
note: Reverberation set by revolving double-sided panels (reflective or absorbing) on the side walls and ceiling; conditions T60_100ms, T60_300ms and T60_600ms (T60 measured with a B&K 2250 meter and a B&K 4295 omni source); volume from the stated size. Source = JBL Go loudspeaker on a 46 x 36 x 32 cm grid (2 cm steps in x and y, 4 cm in z; key x_y_z in mm from the grid corner; the grid centre at 1.15 m height), facing along the y axis. Receivers = six linear arrays of 5 AKG CK32 microphones (-13, -5, 0, +5, +13 cm; mic_0 to mic_4), 1.15 m high, facing the grid centre: array-01 to array-03 in front of the grid at 1, 2 and 3 m, array-04 to array-06 at -45 degrees at the same distances (order from the direct-sound delays). IRs estimated by the authors from the excitation (time-domain least squares), 16 kHz, 0.128/0.256/0.512 s long. The same lab as MIRD and dEchorate; Measured T30: 0.10 s at 1 kHz and about 0.2 s at 500 Hz in T60_100ms (rt_mid 0.15 s), 0.25 s from 250 Hz to 4 kHz in T60_300ms, 0.56 s at mid frequencies in T60_600ms; the authors' 100, 300 and 600 ms are nominal settings read with a sound level meter. The T60_100ms IRs are 0.128 s long, which cuts the 500 Hz decay about 35 dB down: all are graded C and two thirds have no rt_mid
